questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Mandatory part of my study plan. I preferred TUD due to its management courses

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Really easy, we got every useful information months before our arrival either by mail, zoom meetings and previous batch students

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
We were followed throughout the whole introduction period. 
Two tud students welcomed us in person for two days straight, showing us the city, campus and mensa

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was in a student dorm of TUD; they set meetings to help us with the application (for the dorm's rooms)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Dorms are old, not extremely well equipped, but not extremely bad. 
The one I lived in (Budapester strasse 22) was in a strategic postition (close to trains, buses and supermarket)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They have moquette on the floor and overall is not extremely pleasant to be honest

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Organization works in my opinion

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I was already enrolled as part of the GLORFOR master, so I simply chose the univeristy at the beginning of my master (October 2024)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Tutors and some professors (Dr. Auch)

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: This was a very easy step

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I wouldn't really know, because, as I said, it was a compulsory step (Global Forestry is a unique master).
I don't know it usually is. For me it was a really quick and easy

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some of the courses were too basic in my opinion

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Mixed level, since it's a interdisciplinary course. Some of them were too basic for a Master degree

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
More boring, overall less engaging. Less activitities, more old school teaching style. 
Do not expect the danish approach

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Organizations and management 
Economics and management of forest resources
Forest Plantation Silviculture and Agroforestry in the Tropics
Glofor fieldcourse

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
forest economics, amazing professor (Mr. Peter Deegen).
Down to earth Professor and very passionate about the subject. Blends economics, market dynamics and equations with forestry.

Food DKK per month *

questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Probably "good" food, especially if compared to my home country. 
Compared to KU or life in Denmark, everything is cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Honestly, aside from gym and football, I didn't explore much from the university offers.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I only took part to some museums exibitions and football course

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I loved both football course and the TUD gym, but I was there on spring-summer

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I don't know. I was always with my friends, walking around town or biking. Pubs on the weekends are fun

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I'm european and I had already been in Germany, so pretty immediate

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just attend student events! I met many special people there

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No particular challenges

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
If they can choose I'd opt for a different university. Forestry: Wegeningen? 
If you can't choose: it's not too bad, but there's better options. I wouldn't recommend it, but if it happens to be your only choice, don't worry, Tharandt is beautiful

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My GLOFOR buddies, amazing people and Campus in Tharandt

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Speaking German, locals have a low english level

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
